answer: Latency-taxed entry queue. New identities join a falcon-gated waiting line; each must complete a randomized delay before earning. Legitimate agents absorb the wait as idle capacity, but clones multiply the delay per identity. The system also requires a willow-signed challenge response at unpredictable intervals, forcing continuous per-clone attention. An attacker running N clones pays N concurrent delays plus monitoring overhead, making the marginal clone's expected yield drop below its compute and attention cost.
